_comment: Hand-authored citation registry for the Works cited appendix. entries: MLA fields plus a hand-written 'about' line per work; the appendix assembles itself from each lesson's links (rehype-lesson-citations) and looks them up here. pending: cited URLs whose bibliographic facts are still being verified -- they render nothing until moved into entries; never promote one unchecked (empty right now, and kept so a future citation can wait honestly). excluded: links that are not works (course tools, shared working documents). citations.test.ts holds all three sets honest.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.13625.title: Oversight for Frontier AI through a Know-Your-Customer Scheme for Compute Providers
https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.13625.about: A policy paper proposing that compute providers run know-your-customer checks so governments can oversee frontier AI development.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.10748.title: An International Treaty to Implement a Global Compute Cap for Advanced Artificial Intelligence
https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.10748.about: A treaty proposal for a global cap on the computational power used to develop advanced AI, with enforcement machinery.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08797.title: Computing Power and the Governance of Artificial Intelligence
https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08797.about: The foundational survey of compute as a governance lever — why computing power is detectable, excludable, and quantifiable in ways algorithms and data are not.
https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08797.authors: Sastry, Girish, Lennart Heim, Haydn Belfield, et al.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.05812.title: Algorithmic Progress in Language Models
https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.05812.about: An empirical study of 200+ language-model results finding the compute needed for a fixed capability halves roughly every eight months through algorithmic progress.
https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.05812.authors: Ho, Anson, Tamay Besiroglu, Ege Erdil, et al.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.08501.title: Governing Through the Cloud: The Intermediary Role of Compute Providers in AI Regulation
https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.08501.about: A paper on cloud compute providers as regulatory intermediaries — securers, record keepers, verifiers, and enforcers of AI rules.
https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.08501.authors: Heim, Lennart, Tim Fist, Janet Egan, et al.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.18308.title: Near-Term Enforcement of AI Chip Export Controls Using a Firmware-Based Design for Offline Licensing
https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.18308.about: A design for firmware-based offline licensing that would disable AI chips lacking a regulatory license, as a near-term export-control enforcement mechanism.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.16074.title: Verification Methods for International AI Agreements

https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03742.title: Hardware-Enabled Mechanisms for Verifying Responsible AI Development

https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03742.authors: O'Gara, Aidan, Gabriel Kulp, Will Hodgkins, et al.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.10618.title: Compute Requirements for Algorithmic Innovation in Frontier AI Models
https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.10618.about: An analysis of 36 algorithmic innovations asking how much compute it takes to invent frontier-model improvements, and whether compute restrictions would slow them.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.15916.about: The six-layer verification framework this module leans on: independent layers from chip-level security to whistleblower programs for verifying AI agreements.
https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.15916.authors: Baker, Mauricio, Gabriel Kulp, Oliver Marks, et al.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.10783.title: An International Agreement to Prevent the Premature Creation of Artificial Superintelligence
